raw_extraction.description: Brex is the first fully unified spend platform with global corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, travel, and bill pay. It enables finance teams to control all of their spend in one place. The Brex API uses REST architecture, is defined using the OpenAPI specification, uses standard HTTP response codes and verbs, accepts and returns JSON, and requires HTTPS. The API includes endpoints for accounting, budgets, expenses, fields, onboarding, payments, team management, transactions, travel, and webhooks.
raw_extraction.api_breadth: The API covers a wide range of financial management functions including accounting, budgets, expenses, fields, onboarding, payments, team management, transactions, travel, and webhooks.
raw_extraction.mcp_notes: Brex provides an official MCP (Managed Customer Portal) as indicated by the presence of a developer dashboard for token management and API usage.
raw_extraction.buildability_rationale: The API is well documented with a clear authentication method using bearer tokens generated from the Brex dashboard. The API is RESTful, uses standard HTTP methods and JSON, and has comprehensive coverage of financial management features, making it feasible to build integrations.

Generate a user token Sign in to dashboard.brex.com as an account admin or card admin . Go to Developer > Settings . If your company has not accepted the developer API agreement, please review the terms and conditions. These must be accepted to use the developer API. Click Create Token . Create a name for your token that will help you identify it. Choose what level of data access you need for your application; these are the scopes your token will have. The next screen will confirm your previous selections. Make sure it looks good, then select Allow Access . Your token is now created. Copy and store the token securely. You won't be able to see it again. Back on the developer page of your Brex dashboard, you should see your token listed now. As a security measure, part of the string is obfuscated. If you lose it, create a new one and replace the token. Caution : Your user token is private and should not be shared. Never check it into version control or save it somewhere publicly accessible. If your user token is compromised or leaked, make sure to revoke it. 2. Pass the user token in your API call headers To pass your user token to Brex APIs, add it as a header to your API calls in the following format: Authorization: "Bearer {{your user_token here}}" If, for example, your user token value is bxt_jBWQLZXtu1f4sVT6UjaWPp7Gh9nVGjzEZgRX , your header will be: Authorization: "Bearer bxt_jBWQLZXtu1f4sVT6UjaWPp7Gh9nVGjzEZgRX" Token revocation and expiration There are two scenarios where tokens will be invalid for authentication: User tokens will expire if they are not used to make an API call for 90 days User tokens associated to users in a non-active status will no longer work If your token is compromised, or you no longer need it, revoke the user token from the developer page in your Brex dashboard. Once revoked, any calls made with this token will immediately begin to fail. API Server Brex currently only offers a production API server at https://api.brex.com . This is the base URL for all API calls. Was this helpful? Previous page Quickstart Next page Partner authentication Copyright © Brex LLC 2019–2026. All rights reserved. Ask AI
